# Methods

Fictional example used to test the validator.

## Topic 1: Replication and design

**What the paper does.** Six plots per treatment in a randomized complete block design (Methods; Fig. 1).

**What standard practice requires.** Randomization within blocks and a stated unit of replication. A handbook of field-trial design is the usual reference [C-003]; it could not be opened in this run, so this sentence rests on an unverified source.

**Assessment.** Sound.

**Claims affected.** None.

**What would close it.** Nothing needed.

## Topic 2: Measuring the proposed cause

**What the paper does.** Attributes the yield gain to reduced evaporation without measuring soil moisture (Methods; Discussion).

**What standard practice requires.** A causal claim is backed by a measurement of the proposed cause, with the main alternatives controlled.

**Assessment.** Gap. The outcome is measured; the mechanism is not.

**Claims affected.** B-02.

**What would close it.** Soil-moisture readings in both treatments, and plots that separate weed suppression from moisture retention.

## Checklist close-out

| Item | Question | Answer | Where addressed |
|---|---|---|---|
| P-1 | Is the reported effect larger than the variation between replicate plots? | complies | claim B-01 |
| P-2 | Is the claimed cause measured directly, or inferred from the outcome? | departs | claim B-02; Topic 2 |
| P-3 | Are sample size and the unit of replication stated? | complies | claim A-01; Topic 1 |
| P-4 | Is supplementary material that claims depend on available? | departs | claim B-04 |

## Effect on verdicts

|---|---|---|---|---|
